title: Mountains carved the rhythm of our weather
description: The rise of the Himalayan range did more than reshape geography. It triggered a global cooling cycle that fundamentally altered Earth's entire climate system.
instagram_caption: Discover how the peak of the world dictated the pulse of our planet. Follow Wonders of the Nature for more.

segments.narration: These jagged peaks look like solid stone, but they breathe cold global change.
Before they rose, warm winds flowed freely across the center of our planet.
India smashed into Asia, forcing the earth to buckle and reach toward space.
The sudden barrier blocked ancient moisture, forcing the air to drop its burden.
Rain lashed the slopes, stripping away minerals from the freshly broken mountain stone.
This chemical reaction locked carbon dioxide into the soil and the deep sea.
With the carbon trapped, the planet lost its blanket and began to cool.
Ice sheets crept further south, carving valleys into the surface of the world.
Today, those silent giants still dictate the cycle of our global weather patterns.
The world shifted forever, so subscribe to Wonders of the Nature for more.
